title: Tauri 2 Control Room skeleton, read-only, Windows first (lean: no Vite, no Tauri CLI, no React, no Stop)
dependency_notes: CR-01 (orcel-app-api/1, the endpoint read) and CR-02 (the headless client in apps/orcel-control-room, whose reducer and validators the front end reuses) are merged backlog work with no SpecGrain spec of their own; SG-000118 was only their proposed grain. SG-000122 is the founder's sequencing gate (forms on real Edge 157). SG-000126 serves task.list and task.get, which stay outside the first allowlist unless the founder answers question 5 of the prep packet yes. FD-03 is answered by the founder's Decision 4.
objective: Give Orcel a read-only Control Room window built on Tauri 2, written lean: no Vite, no Tauri CLI, no React, configuration written from scratch, no Stop control. The Tauri Rust process is the only client of orceld's local app API (orcel-app-api/1): it opens this user's endpoint as an identification-only client, confirms the server runs as this user, and sends only status.get, capabilities.get and events.subscribe. The web view shows status, capabilities with explicit unavailable reasons, the device list as unavailable, and the event timeline, through three typed Tauri commands under a strict CSP with embedded assets only. orceld remains the sole authority; the window answers no approval and changes no state. Native evidence on Windows (WebView2) in this grain; macOS and Linux compile-only legs are optional; development builds only. This is the draft of docs/orcel/implementation-readiness/prep/SG-000119.md and activates nothing.

include: Activate the SG-000119 contract only (slice A0). Every slice below needs its own exact-head qualified implementation PR with the review gates and a fresh-context security judge.

Slice A1, the Rust app API client: crates/orcel-app-api-client in the root workspace, using only std, windows-sys 0.52 and libc already in the root lock. Windows: open \\.\pipe\orcel-<user SID>-app with SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION, read GetNamedPipeServerProcessId, and require the server's token user to equal this process's and its integrity to be Medium or above before the first write (lifted from orceld's describe_holder and token_user). macOS and Linux: the no-follow directory and socket ownership checks of the TypeScript client. A closed method enum of status.get, capabilities.get and events.subscribe; 64 KiB frames; epoch-aware cursors with gap rejection before the cursor moves.

Slice A2, the Tauri skeleton: apps/orcel-control-room/src-tauri as its own Cargo workspace with its own Cargo.lock, deny.toml and notices, excluded from the root workspace; tauri and tauri-build pinned exactly with default-features off and only wry and custom-protocol on; tauri.conf.json and one capability file written from scratch; embedded assets, the recorded CSP, navigation and new-window refusal, drag-drop off, devtools off, refusal to start when any WEBVIEW2_* environment variable is set, an explicit WebView2 user data folder outside orceld's state root; a static not-connected page. This slice is the first download and needs the founder's download approval.

Slice A3, the bridge: three Tauri commands, app_status, app_capabilities and app_events (a tauri::ipc::Channel stream), over A1; permissions generated by tauri_build AppManifest for exactly these three; invoke_handler registers exactly these three.

Slice A4, the view: plain HTML, CSS and TypeScript compiled by the typescript 5.9.3 already locked in apps/orcel-control-room, no bundler; status, capabilities with unavailable reasons, the device list shown unavailable (devices.list is reserved), the timeline from events using the headless client's reducer; pending approvals shown only as waiting for approval on this device; every field rendered as text.

Slice A5, accessibility and the Windows run: keyboard-only use, screen reader names, RTL layout, 100/150/200% scaling, UI Automation checks adapted from PR #282's checks that apply to a read-only view, native evidence that the WebView2 renderer cannot open the pipe, and measurements of cold and warm start, working set and binary size beside the WPF preview for CR-04.

Slice A6 (optional, only with its own download approval): macOS and Linux compile and unit-test CI legs for src-tauri, with the WebKitGTK 4.1 development packages from apt on Linux; no native qualification on either.
Slice A7, closeout: canonical evidence, the resolved crate versions and the known limits.
exclude: Stop of any kind: task.stop, emergency revoke, Stop desktop control, or any control that changes orceld state.
task.list and task.get unless the founder answers prep packet question 5 yes; approval.history, clients.list and every other app API method.
Answering, cancelling, minting or forwarding an approval; any affordance that looks like one.
React, Vite, the Tauri CLI, tauri-driver, msedgedriver, @tauri-apps/api or any other npm package not already locked; the AgentKit React components and @tabler/icons-react.
Copying Cua Spaces' src-tauri scaffolding (FSL) or the cua-driver Tauri fixture's main.rs, tauri.conf.json or tiny_http server; the fixture itself is unchanged.
Any Tauri plugin (shell, fs, http, dialog, opener, process, updater, clipboard, notification, global-shortcut, deep-link, store or other).
Remote content, a devUrl, a dev server, any listener, remote IPC access, devtools in release-profile builds, additional WebView2 browser arguments, and macOSPrivateApi.
Installers, bundles, updater artifacts, code signing and the release payload; bundle.active stays false.
Native qualification on macOS and Linux, and any Linux build that runs before WebKitGTK's web process is shown unable to reach the app API socket.
Retiring the WPF preview (CR-04) or changing it.

authority_delta.activation: None. This packet authorizes implementing and proving SG-000119; it adds no dependency, command, listener or authority by itself.
authority_delta.app_api: None. The Control Room is a new client of the existing orcel-app-api/1 endpoint, sending only status.get, capabilities.get and events.subscribe; no method is added to orceld and task.stop is not sent.
authority_delta.ui: Proposed only (slices A2 to A5): a read-only Tauri window whose web view can invoke exactly three commands that return validated read results. It shows pending approvals as waiting for approval on this device and cannot answer them.
authority_delta.dependencies: Proposed only (slice A2, founder download approval): the Tauri 2 crate graph in a separate workspace with an exact-pinned lock, and the system web view (WebView2 on Windows). Slice A1 adds no dependency.
authority_delta.network: None. No listener, no remote content, no connect-src beyond Tauri's IPC origin, no remote IPC.
authority_delta.process: One new unprivileged per-user desktop process and the system web view's own processes; none is spawned by orceld.
authority_delta.approval: None. Approvals stay with the OS presence surfaces.
authority_delta.release: None. Development builds only; nothing enters the release payload.
authority_delta.privileged: None. SG-000096 Full User shell remains unarmed.

invariants: orceld remains the sole approval and execution authority; the Control Room reads and displays only.

The Tauri Rust process is the only app API client; on Windows it opens the pipe as an identification-only client and confirms the server's token user equals its own and its integrity is Medium or above before the first write.
Only status.get, capabilities.get and events.subscribe can be sent (plus task.list and task.get only if the founder approves); the method set is a closed enum, not a string allowlist.

The web view can invoke exactly app_status, app_capabilities and app_events; the capability file grants exactly their three permissions to the main window; no core default permission, no remote section, no plugin.

The CSP is default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; connect-src ipc: http://ipc.localhost; frame-src 'none'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none', narrowed only by evidence; no unsafe source.

Assets are embedded; there is no devUrl, dev server or listener; navigation away from Tauri's asset origin and new windows are refused; drag-drop is off; devtools are absent from release-profile builds.
The process refuses to start when any WEBVIEW2_* environment variable is set and passes no additional browser arguments.
Every field from orceld is rendered as text; no HTML sink, eval or Function exists in the front end.
No control answers, cancels or mints an approval, and no control changes orceld state.
src-tauri is its own workspace with exact pins, a checked-in Cargo.lock, cargo deny licenses and cargo audit; root builds and the release payload never include it.
Development builds only; bundle.active is false; no updater, installer or signing.
acceptance: Activation (A0): this spec, CURRENT.md's record of the founder go-ahead and Decision 4, and the open-grain pins land together; no code or dependency changes.

Client tests (A1): against a real orceld on the Windows, macOS and Linux legs, each allowed method answers; an unlisted method cannot be constructed; an over-cap frame is refused; a gap is rejected before the cursor moves; a new epoch clears the timeline; daemon down answers a typed unavailable; on Windows a pipe served by another account or below Medium integrity is refused before any write.

Skeleton tests (A2): a Rust test asserts the exact CSP, the capability file's single window and permission list, no remote section, no devUrl and bundle inactive; the navigation predicate refuses https:, http://127.0.0.1, file:, data: and javascript: and allows only the asset origin; cargo tree shows no tauri-plugin-* and no listener crate; cargo deny licenses passes; a WEBVIEW2_* variable stops startup with a stated reason.

Bridge tests (A3): the AppManifest command list and the invoke_handler list are equal; an unknown command invoked from the page is refused by the ACL; an extra argument is refused; the event Channel ends when the window closes.

View tests (A4): the reducer's gap, duplicate and epoch cases pass on the compiled modules; a static check finds no innerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, eval, Function or inline handler; no element answers an approval; control and bidi characters are replaced.

Windows run (A5): UI Automation checks pass on windows-latest and on the founder's PC through a live orceld; keyboard-only and Narrator checks recorded; the renderer is shown unable to open the pipe; start, memory and size measured beside the WPF preview; each run records its WebView2 version.
Optional legs (A6): the A2 and A3 Rust tests pass on macOS and Linux.
Closeout (A7): canonical evidence, the resolved versions written into this spec and the prep packet, the known limits.
